title: One refiner: every sentence you say lands in a task
description: A plan, not built: keep one of the 8 prompt refiners, write down what each one does well, and place every sentence into a task on all three channels. Waits for your yes.

add.text:
**The plan in one line:** every prompt, typed or spoken, goes through one writer that numbers its sentences, then one refiner (Sonnet) splits it into asks, and each ask becomes a task that cites its sentences. Coverage is then a count: sentences cited by a task, out of all sentences. **Study only: nothing retires or changes until you say yes.**

**This week (2026-11-01 to 11-08, 298 of your prompts): coverage is 0% on every channel.** No sentence you said this week is placed in a task by code. The one step that did this (PromptTasks) is switched off, and the cloud voice record does not store your words at all.
1. The 8 refiners, and the one thing each does best

add.title: Hook (prompt-relay): live, saves every VS Code prompt
add.description: Lesson: no model call, so nothing you type is ever missed.
add.text:
**Path:** `.claude/hooks/prompt-relay.mjs` (registered in `.claude/settings.json:251`)

```js
hook(prompt) → Ask.write(text) → Prompt task + numbered sentences on the session
```

**Who calls it:** Claude Code, on every prompt in a VS Code tab. **Live.**

**Lesson:** it is code, not a model, and it runs on every prompt, so capture can never fail for cost or quota. Keep it as the VS Code door.

add.title: PromptTasks + PromptRecords live: off since 11-02
add.description: Lesson: the only one that turns an ask into a task that points back at its sentences.
add.text:
**Path:** `Servex/agents/PromptTasks.js`, `Server/PromptRecords.mjs`

```js
PromptRecords.live(session, prompt) → parts [{id, cites:[3,4], kind:"ask"}]
                                    → tasks {source:{prompt, part}}  // at most 15
```

**Who calls it:** Servex, on each VS Code prompt (`Servex/Servex.js:311`), but it is **switched off** (the `prompt-tasks.off` file in the Servex home). 0 `parts` lines this week; last data 11-02.

**Lesson:** a part cites sentence numbers and a task cites its part (`source.part`). That join is the only existing way to compute coverage. **This is the one to keep.**

add.title: PromptRecords review: manual, the same rules run on a past session
add.description: Lesson: improve the instructions, then rerun them backwards.
add.text:
**Path:** `Server/PromptRecords.mjs` (`--process review`)

```js
PromptRecords.review(session) → parts + what came of each + tasks for asks still open
```

**Who calls it:** a human, from the command line. **Manual.**

**Lesson:** live and review share one brief, so a fix to the rules can be replayed on old sessions. Keep it as the refiner's second timing.

add.title: RefineQueue + RefinedCard: manual, refines from raw transcripts
add.description: Lesson: it reads the raw transcripts, so it catches prompts no hook ever saw.
add.text:
**Path:** `Server/RefineQueue.mjs`, `public/framework/ext/Refine/RefinedCard.js`

```js
RefineQueue.one(turn) → Haiku → RefinedCard {sentences, asks, target} → AskIndex
```

**Who calls it:** a human (`node Server/RefineQueue.mjs --days 7`); `--repeats` finds asks made more than once. **Manual.**

**Lesson:** working from transcripts fills the gaps the live path leaves, and `--repeats` finds what you asked twice. Both move into review (it reads transcripts when a session has no record).

add.title: PromptAudit: manual, lists the sentences no task covers
add.description: Lesson: the closeout check, measured against what the session really did.
add.text:
**Path:** `Server/PromptAudit.mjs`

```js
PromptAudit.run({days: 7}) → per prompt: tasks, questions, statements + which were done
```

**Who calls it:** a human. Its helpers (`prompts`, `locate`, `read`) are imported by PromptRecords. **Manual.**

**Lesson:** it judges each ask against what happened, not what was planned. That becomes `session.coverage()` (a computed number) plus review's outcome step.

add.title: Echo: live, chat turns get the same numbered sentences
add.description: Lesson: one code path in Servex, no extra model call per turn.
add.text:
**Path:** `Servex/agents/Echo.js` (calls `Ask.write` at line 357)

```js
Echo(prompt) → clean() + structure() → Ask.write(text)
```

**Who calls it:** Servex, on an assistant session's chat turn. **Live.**

**Lesson:** routing through `Ask.write` already gives chat the same sentence numbers as VS Code. Its own `clean()`/`structure()` copy is the duplicate (LiveRefine makes the same two calls).

add.title: LiveRefine: live, fills the outline while you talk
add.description: Lesson: you can watch each sentence slide into its card as you speak.
add.text:
**Path:** `Servex/ext/refine/LiveRefine.js` (`POST /api/refine/live`, `Servex/Servex.js:842`)

```js
LiveRefine(session, sentences) → Haiku every few seconds → outline sections on the page
```

**Who calls it:** web dictation (Dictate), live. 38 of 257 dictated sentences this week landed in an outline, but an outline section is not a task, so none counts as placed.

**Lesson:** placement has to be visible in real time. The kept refiner must show that too (step 4 below).

add.title: Day batch tools: manual, backfill a whole day in one command
add.description: Lesson: one command with a dry run, the template for any mass rerun.
add.text:
**Paths:** `Server/refine.mjs`, `Server/refine-days.mjs`, `Server/DayPromptsRefine.mjs`, `Server/refine-litmus.mjs`

```js
node Server/DayPromptsRefine.mjs 2026-10-03 --dry   // preview, then run for real
```

**Who calls them:** a human; newest data 10-04. **Manual, nearly dead.**

**Lessons:** `--dry` before a bulk write; `refine.mjs`'s `coverage.md` traced every sentence to a deliverable; `refine-litmus` compared models side by side. All three become flags on review (`--day`, `--dry`, `--compare`).

add.title: Three capture pieces, not refiners
add.description: Ask.write numbers sentences; Dictate keeps raw rows; ClaudeCodeTranscript reads raw files.
add.text:
These keep your words; none of them splits a prompt into asks.

```js
Ask.write(text)                    // Server/Ask.mjs: redact secrets, split, number a1, a2…
chat.sentences.add({text})         // Servex/agents/ChatWriter.js: each dictated sentence, untouched
ClaudeCodeTranscript.turns(file)   // Server/ClaudeCodeTranscript.mjs: every owner turn in a raw transcript
```

**Lessons:** one shared splitter, so every channel's sentence numbers mean the same thing; raw rows are never edited; a transcript reader exists for when a record is missing. **All three stay.**

Full record, with callers and evidence: [inventory.json](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-session-truth/one-refiner-plan/inventory.json)

add.title: Keep PromptRecords, on Sonnet, fed by Ask.write
add.description: One brief, two timings (live and review); the other seven's lessons become its flags and views.
add.text:
**Kept:** `PromptRecords` (its parts brief), fed by `Ask.write`'s numbered sentences. Why: it is the only one whose output joins to tasks (`source.part`), so coverage is a count, not an opinion. The calibration showed Sonnet finds more asks than Haiku and costs about $0.03 a prompt ([results](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-session-truth/calibration/results.md)).

```js
Ask.write(text)                      // every channel, one splitter → s1, s2, s3…
Refiner.live(session, prompt)        // Sonnet: parts that cite sentences → tasks
Refiner.review(session, {day, dry})  // the same brief, after the fact
session.coverage()                   // computed: sentences cited by a task ÷ all sentences
```

**What the others add to it:**
- From the hook and Echo: capture stays code, no model.
- From RefineQueue: review reads the raw transcript when a session has no record, and keeps `--repeats`.
- From PromptAudit: `session.coverage()` and an uncovered-sentence list at closeout.
- From LiveRefine: the dictation view shows each sentence moving into its task as it is placed.
- From the day tools: `--day`, `--dry` and `--compare` flags.

**Alternatives:** keep LiveRefine (live and visible, but it makes outlines, not tasks, so coverage stays 0); keep RefineQueue (catches everything from transcripts, but only after the fact, and its cards have no task join). Either wins only if live tasks turn out too noisy.
3. How a sentence gets placed, on each channel

add.title: Sentence → prompt → task, on all three channels
add.description: VS Code is one switch away; web dictation needs one call; cloud voice needs your words stored first.
add.text:
```js
const p = Ask.write(text, {via})     // 1. sentences numbered s1…sN on the session
const parts = Refiner.live(session, p) // 2. Sonnet: [{kind:"ask", cites:[1,2]}, …]
session.tasks.add({title, source: {prompt: p.id, part}})  // 3. one task per ask
// existing task first: a missing requirement is added to it, not a near-duplicate
```

| Channel | Prompts this week | Today | What it needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| VS Code | 10 (121 sentences) | hook → Ask.write works; refiner is switched off | turn PromptTasks on, with Sonnet |
| Web dictation | 262 (257 sentences) | raw sentences kept; 38 in an outline, 0 in tasks | at each pause, call Ask.write then the refiner |
| Cloud voice | 26 | your words are not stored, only tool calls | the voice agent logs what you said through Ask.write |

**Coverage this week: 0 of 378 stored sentences placed (0%) on every channel,** plus cloud voice with none stored. Counted by [coverage.mjs](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-session-truth/one-refiner-plan/coverage.mjs); its prompt total (298) equals the mentions count's for the same days.

**After the steps below, coverage would read** as a number per session, e.g. `session.coverage() // 0.94`, with the uncovered sentences listed beside it.
4. Retirement order: small, additive, nothing deleted

add.title: Six steps, about $11 in all
add.description: Lessons are written first; new paths run beside the old; the old ones move to an archive folder last.
add.text:
1. **Write the lessons down** (this page, plus the refinement map updated). About $0.50. Done with this study.
2. **One brief, on Sonnet:** move the parts brief into `ext/Refine/`, switch `PromptRecords.live` to Sonnet, turn PromptTasks on. About $2. This one changes what runs, so it waits for your yes.
3. **`session.coverage()`** computed from sentences, parts and tasks, with its test, shown on the session page. About $2.
4. **Web dictation:** each pause calls `Ask.write`, then the refiner; the view shows sentences moving into tasks. About $3.
5. **Cloud voice:** the voice agent stores your words through `Ask.write` (one MCP call per turn). About $2.
6. **Move aside** RefineQueue's breakdown, PromptAudit's two passes, the day tools and Echo's duplicate clean/structure into an `archive/` folder with a readme of their lessons. LiveRefine goes last, once step 4's view works. About $1.50.

**Risks:**
- Sonnet merged two wants into one ask more often than Haiku on long prompts (6 cases to 2 in the October run).
- Live tasks can be noisy (up to 15 per prompt); existing tasks come first to keep that down.
- Cost: about $0.03 a prompt, so roughly $9 a week at this week's 298 prompts.
- Cloud voice depends on the voice agent passing your words faithfully; a misheard sentence is stored as heard.
